outcomes: Names the conditions of an outpost: protected, not attackable by a pawn
Checks the neighbouring pawns before planting a knight
Explains why a square a pawn can challenge is not an outpost
sources: sources/sheets/nimzowitsch_my-system.md (idea 10: the outpost, e4 v e3 pair)
sources/sheets/znosko-borovsky_middle-game.md (C26 knight, C28 hole; contrast family E)

steps.text: An **outpost** is a square deep in the enemy half that no enemy pawn can ever attack. A piece planted there, usually a knight, is hard to remove and cramps everything around it. A pawn of yours one file over and one rank behind keeps it protected: e4 behind a knight on d5.

steps.caption: Black to move. Watch the knight.

line.say: The knight jumps to d4. The pawn on e5 protects it.
White has no pawn that can attack d4.

steps.text:
Before you plant a piece, check three things.
**Is it protected,** ideally by a pawn?
**Can an enemy pawn attack the square?** Pawns never move backward, so look at the pawns still standing on the neighbouring files.
**Is there something to aim at?**
If a pawn can chase the piece away, you only lose time.

steps.title: Same knight, one pawn different
steps.prompt: Only one Black pawn differs between the two positions. Can a Black pawn drive the knight away from d5? Predict first, then check.
Before you looked at the pawns: did you expect the knight on d5 to be safe? Which pawn did you check first?

steps.text: **Remember.** An outpost is a square deep in enemy territory that no enemy pawn can ever attack. Ask: is it protected, can a pawn on the neighbouring files attack it, and is there something to aim at? If a pawn can chase your piece away, you only lose time.
